p: וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹמֵר וַיֹּאמֶר יַעֲקֹב יַעֲקֹב וְגוֹמֵר.
— ‘God said to Israel,’ etc.; ‘He said: Jacob, Jacob,’ etc.
הִנֵּה אַחַר דִּכְתִיב וַתְּחִי רוּחַ יַעֲקֹב נִקְרָא בְּכָל הַפָּרָשָׁה בְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל.
— After it says, ‘Jacob's spirit revived,’ he is called Israel throughout the passage:
וַיֹּאמֶר יִשְׂרָאֵל רַב וְגוֹמֵר וַיִּסַּע יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל.
— ‘Israel said: It is enough,’ etc.; ‘Israel journeyed’; ‘God said to Israel.’
וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִקְרָא בְּשֵׁם יַעֲקֹב יַעֲקֹב וְכֵן אַחַר כָּךְ נִקְרָא כַּמָּה פְעָמִים יַעֲקֹב.
— Then he is addressed as ‘Jacob, Jacob,’ and subsequently is called Jacob several times.
וְכֵן כְּשֶׁבָּא עִם בָּנָיו לְמִצְרַיִם כְּתִיב גַּם כֵּן יַעֲקֹב וּבָנָיו.
— Likewise, when he comes to Egypt with his sons, it also says, ‘Jacob and his sons.’
וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִקְרָא יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּבָרִאשׁוֹנָה דִּכְתִיב וַיַּעַל לִקְרַאת יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיֹּאמֶר יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל יוֹסֵף.
— Afterward he is again called Israel as before: ‘He went up to meet Israel’; ‘Israel said to Joseph.’

וְהִנֵּה קוֹדֶם לָזֶה כָּתוּב וַיִּזְבַּח זְבָחִים לֵאלֹהֵי אָבִיו יִצְחָק וּפֵרֵשׁ רַבִּי שְׁלֹמֹה יִצְחָקִי מִבְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה חַיָּיב אָדָם בִּכְבוֹד אָבִיו יוֹתֵר מִכְּבוֹד זְקֵנוֹ לְפִיכָךְ תָּלָה בְּיִצְחָק וְלֹא בְאַבְרָהָם.

— Earlier it says, ‘He offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac.’ Rashi explains, from Bereishit Rabbah: A person is more obligated to honor his father than his grandfather; therefore he associated the offering with Isaac rather than Abraham.

h: Jacob and the Purpose of Creation

p: אָכֵן הָעִנְיָן הוּא דְּיַעֲקֹב מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ הָיָה שָׁלֵם בְּתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה פב) שֶׁאִיקוֹנִין שֶׁלּוֹ קְבוּעָה בְּכִסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד.
— The explanation is that Jacob in himself was utterly perfected, as stated in Bereishit Rabbah, chapter 82: his image is fixed upon the Throne of Glory.
וּפֵרֵשׁ רַבִּי שְׁלֹמֹה יִצְחָקִי עַל פָּסוּק הָבָה אֶת אִשְׁתִּי וְגוֹמֵר וַהֲלֹא קַל שֶׁבַּקַּלִּים אֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר וְכוּלֵּי אֶלָּא לְהוֹלִיד תּוֹלָדוֹת אָמַר כָּךְ.
— Rashi explains the verse, ‘Give me my wife,’ etc.: Surely even the basest person does not speak this way, etc.; rather, he said this in order to beget offspring.
וְהוּא כְּמוֹ לֶעָתִיד שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א קלז סוֹף עַמּוּד ב) עַל פָּסוּק וַהֲסִירוֹתִי וְגוֹמֵר וְנָתַתִּי לָכֶם לֵב בָּשָׂר לֵב לְהוֹצִיא בָּשָׂר.

— This resembles the future state described by the Sages (Zohar I, 137b, end), concerning ‘I shall remove,’ etc., ‘and give you a heart of flesh’: a heart directed toward bringing forth flesh, offspring.
וּכְמוֹ אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן קוֹדֶם הַקִּלְקוּל דִּכְתִיב בּוֹ וְלֹא יִתְבּוֹשָׁשׁוּ שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ שׁוּם צַד תַּאֲוָה גּוּפָנִיִּית.
— And it resembles Adam before the corruption, of whom it is written, ‘They were not ashamed,’ for he had no trace of bodily desire.
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁבִּיקֵּשׁ יַעֲקֹב לֵישֵׁב בְּשַׁלְוָה וְכוּלֵּי וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהָיָה סָבוּר שֶׁנִּשְׁלַם תַּכְלִית מְכוּוָּן הַבְּרִיאָה כִּרְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
— The Sages said that Jacob sought to dwell in tranquility, etc.; he thought that creation's intended purpose had been fulfilled according to His blessed will.
קָפַץ עָלָיו רָגְזוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף שֶׁנָּפַל עָלָיו פַּחַד מִבְּחִינַת יוֹסֵף שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַן עֲדַיִין פְּגַם אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן.
— Then Joseph's anguish sprang upon him: fear fell upon him concerning the aspect of Joseph, that Adam's blemish had not yet been rectified.
וּכְשֶׁנִּתְבַּשֵּׂר בִּבְשׂוֹרַת יוֹסֵף כְּתִיב וַתְּחִי רוּחַ יַעֲקֹב.
— When he received the news about Joseph, it says, ‘Jacob's spirit revived.’

h: Torah and the Fear of Exile

p: אָמְנָם כְּשֶׁרָאָה שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לֵירֵד עִם בָּנָיו לְמִצְרַיִם וְשֶׁיַּתְחִיל גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם שֶׁהוּא לְתִיקּוּן קִלְקוּל הַק״ל שָׁנָה מֵאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן וּפְגַם דּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל שֶׁהָיָה בִּפְגַם הַבְּרִית.

— Yet he saw that he must descend to Egypt with his sons and that the Egyptian exile would begin, to rectify the corruption of Adam's 130 years and the blemish of the generation of the Flood, which concerned the covenant.

וּמִדַּת יַעֲקֹב הָיָה תּוֹרָה וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא) עַל פָּסוּק וְאֶת יְהוּדָה שָׁלַח לְפָנָיו לְהַתְקִין לוֹ בֵּית תַּלְמוּד וְעִיקַּר תִּיקּוּן הַבְּרִית עַל יְדֵי הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בְּעֵסֶק הַתּוֹרָה.

— Jacob's attribute was Torah. As Midrash Tanchuma explains the verse, ‘He sent Judah before him’: to establish a house of study. The principal rectification of the covenant comes through diligent engagement in Torah.

וּבְמִצְרַיִם שֶׁיִּהְיוּ בָנָיו בְּגָלוּת וְלֹא יִהְיוּ פְנוּיִם לַעֲסוֹק בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה הָיָה יָרֵא שֶׁיִּשְׁלוֹט בָּהֶם הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א רב א) דְּהָא לֵית לָךְ מִלָּה לְתַבְּרָא יֵצֶר הָרָע אֶלָּא אוֹרַיְיתָא.

— In Egypt, where his sons would be exiled and would lack the leisure to study Torah, he feared that the evil inclination would rule over them. As the holy Zohar says (I, 202a), nothing breaks the evil inclination except Torah.
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁבָּרָא הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע אָמַר וּבָרָאתִי לוֹ תּוֹרָה תַּבְלִין. וְנָפַל עָלָיו הַפַּחַד מִצַּד בִּיטּוּל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בְּמִצְרַיִם.
— Hashem, who created the evil inclination, said, ‘I created Torah as its remedy.’ Thus fear fell upon Jacob concerning the neglect of Torah in Egypt.
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת ס.) פָּחֲדוּ בְצִיּוֹן חַטָּאִים וְהָא כְתִיב אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם מְפַחֵד תָּמִיד אָמַר לוֹ הַהוּא בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּתִיב.
— This parallels the teaching (Berakhot 60a): ‘Sinners in Zion are afraid.’ But does it not say, ‘Happy is the person who always fears’? He replied: That refers to matters of Torah.
הַיְינוּ אַשְׁרֵי מְפַחֵד תָּמִיד שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ בִּטּוּלִים מֵעֵסֶק הַתּוֹרָה.
— That is, happy is one who constantly fears that his engagement in Torah might be interrupted.
וּלְכָךְ כְּתִיב וַיִּזְבַּח זְבָחִים לֵאלֹהֵי אָבִיו יִצְחָק. שֶׁהָיָה מֵעִנְיַן פַּחַד וְיִרְאָה מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה מְפַחֵד שֶׁיִּבָּטְלוּ בָנָיו מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
— Therefore it says, ‘He offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac.’ This concerned fear and reverence, because he feared his sons would be prevented from studying Torah.
וְעַל כֵּן קָרָא לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּזֶה יַעֲקֹב יַעֲקֹב לְרַמֵּז מַדְרֵגַת זַרְעוֹ כְּשֶׁיִּהְיוּ בְּמִצְרַיִם בַּמַּדְרֵיגָה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה.
— Hence the Holy One, blessed be He, addressed him here as ‘Jacob, Jacob,’ alluding to his descendants' lower spiritual state in Egypt.
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנִּדְרַשׁ (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא לג:) וּלְבֵית יַעֲקֹב חַטֹּאתָם אֵלּוּ עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ שֶׁזְּדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוֹת לָהֶם כִּשְׁגָגוֹת.
— This parallels the exposition (Bava Metzia 33b), ‘And to the house of Jacob their sins’: these are the unlearned, whose intentional transgressions are treated as inadvertent.

paragraphs.text: Eruvin 18b: “Rabbi Yirmeyah ben Elazar said: During all the years when Adam was under a ban, he begot spirits, demons, and night spirits, as it says, “Adam lived one hundred and thirty years and begot in his likeness, according to his image”—implying that until then he did not beget according to his image. An objection was raised: Rabbi Meir used to say that Adam was exceedingly pious. When he saw that death had been decreed because of him, he fasted for one hundred and thirty years, separated from his wife for one hundred and thirty years, and wore girdles of fig leaves upon his flesh for one hundred and thirty years. When we said that he begot those beings, we meant through semen emitted involuntarily.”

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Vayigash 11: ““He sent Yehudah ahead of him”: to establish a house of study for him, where he would give instruction and teach the tribes. Know that it was so: when Yosef left him, he knew the passage in which they had parted, for he had been teaching him. When Yosef’s brothers came and said, “Yosef is still alive,” his heart grew faint, for he did not believe them. Yaakov remembered that they had parted while studying the passage of the heifer whose neck is broken, and said: “Let him give you a sign of the passage in which we parted, and I will believe you.” Yosef too remembered it and gave them wagons. When Yaakov saw the wagons, immediately “the spirit of Yaakov their father revived.” This teaches that wherever he went, he engaged in Torah, as his fathers had done.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Ramban, Bereishis 46:1: “Rashi’s explanation is not sufficient. … But this verse contains a secret, which they revealed to us in Bereishit Rabbah: when Jacob came to go down to Egypt, he saw that the exile would begin with him and his descendants, and he was afraid of it. So he offered many sacrifices to the Fear of his father Isaac, so that the attribute of judgment would not be stretched out against him. He did this in Beer Sheba, the house of prayer of his fathers. … Scripture says ‘sacrifices’ to tell us that they were not burnt-offerings like his fathers’; but Jacob, out of fear of Hashem, offered peace-offerings, to bring all the attributes into peace toward him. … His first intention was toward the attribute of might, which is closest to him. … Through the merit of the offerings, the God of his father Isaac appeared to him in visions of the night, with the attribute of judgment softened, and He promised him that he need not fear in Egypt, for he would prevail in his judgment and be redeemed after the affliction; this is the meaning of ‘and I shall also surely bring you up.’”

h: The Promise of Ascent from Egypt

p: וְאָמַר לוֹ דְּאַף עַל פִּי כֵן אַל תִּירָא מֵרְדָה מִצְרַיְמָה. וְאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה עו) אֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר אַל תִּירָא אֶלָּא לְמִי שֶׁנִּתְיָירֵא.
— He told him: Nevertheless, ‘Do not fear to descend to Egypt.’ The Sages said (Bereishit Rabbah, chapter 76): ‘Do not fear’ is said only to someone who has become afraid.

וְכֵן יַעֲקֹב נִתְיָירֵא מִצַּד בָּנָיו וְזַרְעוֹ שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לְהִבָּטֵל מִן הַתּוֹרָה בְּמִצְרַיִם וְאָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אַל תִּירָא מֵרְדָה מִצְרַיְמָה וְגוֹמֵר אָנֹכִי אֵרֵד עִמְּךָ.

— Jacob likewise feared on account of his sons and descendants, who might be kept from Torah in Egypt. The Holy One, blessed be He, told him, ‘Do not fear to descend to Egypt,’ etc., ‘I shall descend with you.’
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאֶהְיֶה עִמָּהֶם בְּמִצְרַיִם וְאָנֹכִי אַעַלְךָ גַם עָלֹה כִּי דַיְיקָא מִשָּׁם יִהְיֶה לָהֶם עֲלִיָּה גְדוֹלָה.
— That is, I shall be with them in Egypt, ‘and I shall also surely bring you up,’ for precisely from there they will attain a great ascent.
כִּי שָׁם זָכוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהִשִּׂיגוּ בְּחִינַת הָאַהֲבָה וְהַחֶסֶד בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת כְּדִכְתִיב זָכַרְתִּי לָךְ חֶסֶד נְעוּרַיִךְ וְגוֹמֵר.
— For there Israel merited and attained the expansive expression of love and kindness, as it is written, ‘I remember for you the kindness of your youth,’ etc.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Mei HaShiloach II, Vayigash §3: “Jacob feared descending to Egypt until God told him, ‘Do not fear.’ The reason is the teaching, ‘There is no Torah like the Torah of the Land of Israel’; the lands outside it are not worthy for the Torah to be given to Israel there. This was Jacob’s fear, until God promised him, ‘I—Anokhi—will descend with you to Egypt.’ The word Anokhi alludes to the Torah: even outside the Land, God would impart words of Torah to him. Jacob further feared that, since holiness is not as manifest outside the Land, the Torah imparted there would not contain as much holiness. God promised him, ‘I will also surely bring you up’: he would reach the highest level of Torah. This is the allusion of ‘also bring you up.’”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Mei HaShiloach identifies Anokhi specifically with Torah and distinguishes two fears: losing Torah in exile and receiving it at a diminished level. The promise answers both, thereby explaining why the manuscript speaks of a greater ascent arising precisely from Egypt.

p: וְיוֹסֵף יָשִׁית יָדוֹ עַל עֵינֶיךָ הַיְינוּ שֶׁיְּתַקְּנוּ בְּמִצְרַיִם עִנְיַן פְּגַם הַבְּרִית.
— ‘Joseph shall place his hand upon your eyes’ means that in Egypt they will rectify the blemish of the covenant.
כִּי עֵינַיִם הֵם סַרְסוּרֵי דַּחֲטָאָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב יְרוּשַׁלְמִי פֶּרֶק א דִּבְרָכוֹת הֲלָכָה ה). וּכְמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ (בְּרָכוֹת יב:) אַחֲרֵי עֵינֵיכֶם זֶה הִרְהוּר עֲבֵירָה.
— For the eyes are agents of sin (Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot 1:5), as the Sages expounded (Berakhot 12b), ‘after your eyes’ refers to sinful thoughts.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְיוֹסֵף יָשִׁית יָדוֹ עַל עֵינֶיךָ שֶׁקְּדוּשַּׁת יוֹסֵף יוֹעִיל שֶׁיִּגְדְּרוּ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַצְמָן בִּקְדוּשַּׁת הַבְּרִית.
— Thus ‘Joseph shall place his hand upon your eyes’ means that Joseph's holiness will enable all Israel to safeguard themselves in the holiness of the covenant.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ד) יוֹסֵף יָרַד לְמִצְרַיִם וְגָדַר עַצְמוֹ מִן הָעֶרְוָה וְנִגְדְּרוּ כָּל הַזְּכָרִים בִּזְכוּתוֹ.
— As it is taught (Shir HaShirim Rabbah, chapter 4), Joseph descended to Egypt and safeguarded himself from sexual immorality, and all the males safeguarded themselves through his merit.
וּבֶאֱמֶת הָיוּ גְדוּרִים מִן הָעֶרְוָה בְּמִצְרַיִם וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם שֶׁבִּזְכוּת גְּדִירַת הָעֶרְוָה נִגְאֲלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּצְרַיִם:
— Indeed, they safeguarded themselves from sexual immorality in Egypt; as stated there, Israel were redeemed from Egypt through the merit of this restraint.

paragraphs.text: Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:12: “Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: Sarah went down to Egypt and guarded herself against sexual immorality, and all the women guarded themselves through her merit. Yosef went down to Egypt and guarded himself against sexual immorality, and all the men guarded themselves through his merit. Rabbi Pinchas said in Rabbi Chiya’s name: The restraint against sexual immorality was itself sufficient for Israel to be redeemed from Egypt through its merit. What is the reason? “A locked garden is my sister, my bride.” What is written afterward? “Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates.””
